# DuckDB Data Agent

> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.

[![Deploy to Render](https://render.com/images/deploy-to-render-button.svg)](https://render.com/deploy)

A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.

## Features

### SQL Playground

- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types

### AI Agent

- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)

### Installation

```bash
make install
```

Or install frontend and backend separately:

```bash
cd frontend && npm install
cd backend && poetry install
```

### Configuration

Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
```

Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
```

> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.

### Development

Start both the frontend and backend:

```bash
make dev
```

Or run them separately:

```bash
make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
make backend    # http://localhost:8000
```

Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.

## Production Build and Deployment

The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.

### Build and run locally

```bash
docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
docker run -p 10000:10000 -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... duckdb-data-agent
```

Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.

### Deploy to Render

A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`).

Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.

## Project Structure

```
├── frontend/               # React frontend
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)
│   │   ├── agent/          #   Agent service (SSE event handling)
│   │   ├── AgentContext.tsx #   Agent state management
│   │   └── types.ts        #   Shared TypeScript interfaces
│   ├── index.html          #   HTML entry point
│   ├── package.json        #   npm config
│   └── vite.config.ts      #   Vite bundler config
├── backend/                # FastAPI backend
│   └── app/
│       ├── main.py         #   App setup & CORS
│       ├── config.py       #   Environment variables (API key, model)
│       ├── database.py     #   DuckDB connection & query execution
│       ├── agent.py        #   Agent loop & SSE streaming

   272→    accumulated_answer = ""

1→# Langfuse Integration Design
     2→
     3→## Goal
     4→
     5→Add Langfuse observability tracing to the agent backend and a "Langfuse Traces" button to the agent mode UI. Langfuse is optional — when not configured, tracing is skipped with zero overhead and the button is shown disabled.
     6→
     7→## Approach
     8→
     9→**@observe decorator + manual spans** — wraps the existing `stream_chat()` function with Langfuse tracing. Each agent chat request produces one trace containing LLM generation spans and tool execution spans. No changes to the SSE streaming protocol.
    10→
    11→## Backend Changes
    12→
    13→### 1. Configuration (`backend/app/config.py`)
    14→
    15→Add environment variables:
    16→
    17→```python
    18→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY = os.getenv("LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY", "")
    19→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY = os.getenv("LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY", "")
    20→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL = os.getenv("LANGFUSE_BASE_URL", "https://cloud.langfuse.com")
    21→LANGFUSE_ENABLED = bool(LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY and LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY)
    22→```
    23→
    24→Update `backend/.env.example`:

    27→LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=
    28→LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=
    29→LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com
    30→```
    31→
    32→### 2. Tracing Module (`backend/app/tracing.py`)
    33→
    34→New module that:
    35→
    36→- Initializes Langfuse client only when `LANGFUSE_ENABLED` is True
    37→- Verifies connection with `auth_check()` at startup (logs warning on failure)
    38→- Exposes `get_langfuse_client()` returning the client or `None`
    39→- Exposes `get_langfuse_dashboard_url()` returning the base URL or `None`
    40→
    41→### 3. Agent Instrumentation (`backend/app/agent.py`)
    42→
    43→Wrap `stream_chat()` with conditional Langfuse tracing:
    44→
    45→**Trace hierarchy:**
    46→
    47→```
    48→Trace: "agent-chat"
    49→  metadata: { session_id, model, user_message (truncated) }
    50→  ├── Generation: "llm-turn-N"
    51→  │   input: messages context
    52→  │   output: thinking + text content
    53→  │   usage: { input_tokens, output_tokens }
    54→  ├── Span: "tool-execute_sql"
    55→  │   input: { sql }
    56→  │   output: { columns, rows (truncated), rowCount } or { error }
    57→  └── (repeats for multi-turn agent loops)
    58→```
    59→
    60→Key constraints:
    61→- Tracing is conditional — if `get_langfuse_client()` returns `None`, no spans are created
    62→- Zero changes to the SSE event protocol
    63→- Trace captures the session_id as the Langfuse session ID for grouping multi-turn conversations
    64→- Tool results are truncated in traces to avoid sending large datasets to Langfuse
    65→
    66→### 4. API Endpoint (`backend/app/routes/langfuse.py`)
    67→
    68→```
    69→GET /api/langfuse/status
    70→Response: { "enabled": true, "dashboardUrl": "https://cloud.langfuse.com" }
    71→       or { "enabled": false, "dashboardUrl": null }
    72→```
    73→
    74→No secrets exposed. Called once by frontend on app load.
    75→
    76→### 5. App Setup (`backend/app/main.py`)
    77→
    78→Register the new langfuse router.
    79→

    81→
    82→Add `langfuse` package.

    50→    if len(text) <= max_len:
    51→        return text
    52→    return text[:max_len] + "..."
    53→
    54→
    55→def _extract_tool_result_text(content: object) -> str:
    56→    """Extract text from ToolResultBlock.content."""
    57→    if content is None:
    58→        return ""
    59→    if isinstance(content, str):
    60→        return content
    61→    if isinstance(content, list):
    62→        parts = []
    63→        for item in content:
    64→            if isinstance(item, dict) and item.get("type") == "text":
    65→                parts.append(item.get("text", ""))
    66→        return "\n".join(parts)
    67→    return str(content)

    70→async def stream_chat(message: str, session_id: str | None = None) -> AsyncIterator[str]:

    72→    duckdb_server = create_duckdb_server()
    73→
    74→    logger.info("Using model: %s", ANTHROPIC_MODEL)

    76→        model=ANTHROPIC_MODEL,
    77→        system_prompt=build_system_prompt(),
    78→        mcp_servers={"duckdb": duckdb_server},
    79→        allowed_tools=["mcp__duckdb__execute_sql"],
    80→        permission_mode="bypassPermissions",
    81→        max_turns=20,
    82→        include_partial_messages=True,
    83→    )

    92→        try:
    93→            trace = langfuse.start_span(name="agent-chat")
    94→            trace.update_trace(
    95→                session_id=session_id or "default",
    96→                input={"message": _truncate(message, 500)},
    97→                metadata={"model": ANTHROPIC_MODEL},
    98→            )
    99→        except Exception as e:
   100→            logger.debug("Failed to create Langfuse trace: %s", e)
   101→            trace = None
   102→

   104→    current_generation = None
   105→    turn_number = 0
   106→    accumulated_thinking = ""
   107→    accumulated_answer = ""
   108→
   109→    def _end_generation():
   110→        """End the current generation span, recording accumulated text."""
   111→        nonlocal current_generation, accumulated_thinking, accumulated_answer

   113→            try:
   114→                output_data = {}
   115→                if accumulated_thinking:
   116→                    output_data["thinking"] = _truncate(accumulated_thinking)
   117→                if accumulated_answer:
   118→                    output_data["text"] = _truncate(accumulated_answer)
   119→                current_generation.update(output=output_data)
   120→                current_generation.end()
   121→            except Exception as e:

   125→        accumulated_answer = ""

   176→                    delta_type = delta.get("type", "")

## Comprehensive Langfuse Integration Summary

I've thoroughly explored the Langfuse integration in this DuckDB Data Agent project. Here's a complete breakdown of the implementation:

---

### 1. CONFIGURATION (Environment & Settings)

**Backend Configuration Files:**
- **`backend/app/config.py`** - Defines 4 Langfuse environment variables:
  - `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` - Public key for Langfuse authentication (default: empty)
  - `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` - Secret key for Langfuse authentication (default: empty)
  - `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` - Dashboard URL (default: `https://cloud.langfuse.com`)
  - `LANGFUSE_ENABLED` - Boolean flag that's true only when both public and secret keys are set

- **`backend/.env.example`** - Template showing users how to configure:
  ```
  LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=
  LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=
  LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com
  ```

- **`backend/pyproject.toml`** - Lists `langfuse = "^3.0.0"` as a dependency (Python SDK v3)

**Key Design:** Langfuse is completely optional. When env keys are not set, `LANGFUSE_ENABLED` is `False` and tracing is skipped with zero overhead.

---

### 2. BACKEND LANGFUSE CODE

**`backend/app/tracing.py`** - Langfuse client wrapper module:
- **`_init_langfuse()`** - Initializes the Langfuse client on module import
  - Checks if enabled, creates `Langfuse` client with config vars
  - Performs `auth_check()` at startup to verify credentials
  - Logs warnings if auth fails, gracefully disables tracing
- **`get_langfuse_client()`** - Returns the client or `None` if not configured
- **`get_langfuse_dashboard_url()`** - Returns the dashboard URL or `None`

**`backend/app/agent.py`** - Core tracing instrumentation in `stream_chat()` function:

**Trace Hierarchy:**
```
Trace: "agent-chat"
  ├── Generation: "llm-turn-1", "llm-turn-2", ... (one per LLM turn)
  │   input: user message (truncated to 500 chars)
  │   output: thinking + text content (truncated to 1000 chars)
  │   model: ANTHROPIC_MODEL
  │
  ├── Span: "tool-execute_sql" (for each SQL tool execution)
  │   input: { sql }
  │   output: { rowCount, columns } on success OR { error } on failure
  │
  └── Metadata: { session_id, model }
```

**Tracing Features:**
- Uses Langfuse SDK v3 API (`start_span`, `start_generation`, `update`, `end`, `flush`)
- `_start_generation()` - Creates a generation span for each LLM turn
- `_end_generation()` - Ends generation, recording accumulated thinking & answer text
- Tool SQL execution creates spans with `trace.start_span(name=f"tool-{tool_name}")`
- Truncates data to prevent sending large datasets to Langfuse (500 char for messages, 1000 for outputs, 100 rows max)
- Graceful error handling - tracing failures are logged but don't break the agent
- `langfuse.flush()` called in finally block to ensure all data is sent

**Session Grouping:** Each trace uses `session_id` to group multi-turn conversations in Langfuse.

**`backend/app/routes/langfuse_status.py`** - Status API endpoint:
```python
GET /api/langfuse/status
Response: { 
  "enabled": boolean,
  "dashboardUrl": string | null
}
```
No secrets exposed. Called once by frontend on app load.

**`backend/app/main.py`** - Registers the langfuse router:
```python
from app.routes import tables, query, chat, langfuse_status
app.include_router(langfuse_status.router)
```

---

### 3. FRONTEND LANGFUSE UI

**`frontend/src/types.ts`** - Type definitions:
```typescript
export interface LangfuseStatus {
  enabled: boolean;
  dashboardUrl: string | null;
}
```

**`frontend/src/App.tsx`** - Langfuse status fetching:
- Adds `langfuseStatus` state on app load
- Fetches `/api/langfuse/status` during initial load (alongside health check)
- Gracefully handles fetch failures (non-critical)
- Passes `langfuseStatus` through `AppContent` to `AgentPanel`

**`frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.tsx`** - Langfuse Traces button:
- Accepts `langfuseStatus` prop
- Renders button in agent panel header between title and clear button:
  ```
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ Agent Mode    [LF Traces]  [Clear]  │
  ```
- Button states:
  - **Enabled** (when `enabled: true`): Clickable, opens dashboard URL in new tab
  - **Disabled** (when `enabled: false`): Grayed out (opacity 0.4), disabled attribute, tooltip "Langfuse not configured"
- Displays Langfuse logo icon (`/langfuse-color.svg`) next to text
- Click handler uses `window.open(dashboardUrl, '_blank', 'noopener,noreferrer')`

**`frontend/src/components/AgentPanel.css`** - Button styling:
```css
.agent-panel__actions { display: flex; gap: 8px; }

  - `LANGFUSE_BASE_URL` - Dashboard URL (default: `https://cloud.langfuse.com`)
  - `LANGFUSE_ENABLED` - Boolean flag that's true only when both public and secret keys are set

- **`backend/.env.example`** - Template showing users how to configure:
  ```
  LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=
  LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=
  LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com
  ```

- **`backend/pyproject.toml`** - Lists `langfuse = "^3.0.0"` as a dependency (Python SDK v3)

### 2. BACKEND LANGFUSE CODE

**`backend/app/tracing.py`** - Langfuse client wrapper module:
- **`_init_langfuse()`** - Initializes the Langfuse client on module import

  ├── Generation: "llm-turn-1", "llm-turn-2", ... (one per LLM turn)
  │   input: user message (truncated to 500 chars)
  │   output: thinking + text content (truncated to 1000 chars)

# DuckDB Data Agent

> **Note:** This project is built with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code)(using Opus 4.6 and [superpowers](https://github.com/obra/superpowers)) by more than 95% and human-reviewed by author.

A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.

## Features

### SQL Playground

- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types

### AI Agent

- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)

### Installation

```bash
make install
```

Or install frontend and backend separately:

```bash
cd frontend && npm install
cd backend && poetry install
```

### Configuration

Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
```

Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
```

> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.

### Development

Start both the frontend and backend:

```bash
make dev
```

Or run them separately:

```bash
make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
make backend    # http://localhost:8000
```

Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.

## Production Build and Deployment

The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.

### Build and run locally

```bash
docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
docker run -p 10000:10000 -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... duckdb-data-agent
```

Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.

### Deploy to Render

A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`).

Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.

│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── components/     #   UI components (editor, results, sidebar, chat)

- [React](https://react.dev/) 18 + [TypeScript](https://www.typescriptlang.org/)
- [Vite](https://vite.dev/)

**Backend**
- [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) + [Uvicorn](https://www.uvicorn.org/)

# Stage 1: Build frontend
FROM node:20-slim AS frontend-build
WORKDIR /app
COPY frontend/package.json frontend/package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci
COPY frontend/index.html frontend/vite.config.ts frontend/tsconfig.json frontend/tsconfig.app.json frontend/tsconfig.node.json ./
COPY frontend/src/ src/
RUN npm run build

# Stage 2: Python backend
FROM python:3.12-slim
WORKDIR /app

# Install Node.js (required for Claude CLI)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends curl && \
    curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x | bash - && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends nodejs && \
    apt-get clean && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Install Claude CLI globally
RUN npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code

RUN pip install --no-cache-dir poetry && \
    poetry config virtualenvs.create false

COPY backend/pyproject.toml backend/poetry.lock ./
RUN poetry install --no-root --no-interaction

COPY backend/app/ app/

# Copy built frontend into backend static directory
COPY --from=frontend-build /app/dist/ static/

# Create non-root user (Claude CLI refuses --dangerously-skip-permissions as root)
RUN useradd -m appuser
USER appuser

EXPOSE 10000

CMD ["uvicorn", "app.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "10000"]

A SQL playground with an AI-powered data analysis agent. Upload CSV files, write SQL queries, or ask questions in plain English — powered by [DuckDB](https://duckdb.org/) on a lightweight [FastAPI](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/) backend with a React frontend.

## Features

### SQL Playground

- **DuckDB SQL engine** — Fast, in-process analytical database on the backend
- **CSV file upload** — Drag-and-drop or click to import CSV files (up to 500 MB) with automatic schema detection
- **Sample dataset** — One-click load of the Titanic dataset to get started quickly
- **SQL query editor** — Write and execute queries with Ctrl/Cmd+Enter
- **Interactive results** — Sortable columns, per-column filters, and global search across results
- **EXPLAIN support** — Markdown-rendered output for `EXPLAIN` and `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` queries
- **Table sidebar** — Collapsible panel to browse tables, inspect columns, and view types

### AI Agent

- **Natural language queries** — Ask questions about your data in plain English; the agent writes and executes SQL for you
- **Streaming responses** — Real-time token streaming powered by Claude via the [Anthropic Agent SDK](https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python)
- **Visible reasoning** — Collapsible thinking block shows the agent's intermediate steps and SQL queries
- **Inline results** — Query results rendered inline within the conversation
- **Privacy-conscious** — Requires an Anthropic API key stored in a server-side `.env` file; your data and key are never sent anywhere besides the Anthropic API
- **Langfuse observability** (optional) — Built-in [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/) tracing for monitoring agent interactions, with a one-click dashboard link in the UI

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) 20+
- [Python](https://www.python.org/) 3.12+
- [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/)

### Installation

```bash
make install
```

Or install frontend and backend separately:

```bash
cd frontend && npm install
cd backend && poetry install
```

### Configuration

Copy the example environment file and add your Anthropic API key:

```bash
cp backend/.env.example backend/.env
```

Edit `backend/.env` and set your key:

```
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
ANTHROPIC_MODEL=sonnet    # optional, defaults to sonnet
```

> Both variables are only needed for the AI agent. The SQL playground works without them, but both require the backend running.

#### Langfuse (optional)

To enable agent tracing with [Langfuse](https://langfuse.com/), add these to `backend/.env`:

```
LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-...
LANGFUSE_BASE_URL=https://cloud.langfuse.com   # optional, defaults to cloud
```

When configured, every agent conversation is traced (LLM turns, tool calls, SQL execution) and a **Langfuse Traces** button appears in the agent panel header linking to your dashboard. When not configured, tracing is disabled with zero overhead.

### Development

Start both the frontend and backend:

```bash
make dev
```

Or run them separately:

```bash
make frontend   # http://localhost:5173
make backend    # http://localhost:8000
```

Open http://localhost:5173 to use the app. The Vite dev server proxies `/api` requests to the backend automatically.

## Production Build and Deployment

The project ships as a single Docker image that bundles the React frontend and FastAPI backend. A multi-stage `Dockerfile` builds the frontend, then copies the output into the backend's static directory.

### Build and run locally

```bash
docker build -t duckdb-data-agent .
docker run -p 10000:10000 \
  -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY=pk-lf-... \
  -e LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY=sk-lf-... \
  duckdb-data-agent
```

Open http://localhost:10000 to use the app.

### Deploy to Render

A `render.yaml` is included for one-click deployment on [Render](https://render.com/):

1. Push this repo to GitHub.
2. In Render, create a new **Blueprint** and connect the repo.
3. Set the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` environment variable in the Render dashboard. Optionally set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to override the default model (`sonnet`). To enable Langfuse tracing, also set `LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY`.

Render will build the Docker image and deploy it automatically on every push to `main`.
